source.original_title: 06/06/2026 - Dan Sigman x Ben Byrne KL
source.display_title: 06/06/2026 - Dan Sigman x Ben Byrne KL — Follow Up

setter.name: Kyla
setter.evidence: Code taken from the title suffix. The prospect never names the setter; the only corroboration is the rep referencing pre-call notes — 'Well, I got some notes about you. Yeah. Just a little bit.'

prospect.name: Dan Sigman
prospect.occupation: Financial advisor, office-based; has a book of business and plans to work until 70
prospect.family_status: Married; wife follows Trevor on Instagram, likes to hike, does not train the way he does
prospect.training_background: Lifelong weightlifter since roughly age 15, played high-school football. Last couple of years: upper/lower body splits four to five days a week, assault bike, rower, walking. Has already lost a significant amount of fat and believes he kept most of his lean mass. Home gym fully outfitted. Deliberately lifting lighter to protect his joints. Vegetarian for 20 years.
prospect.medical: Shoulder was 'a little bit dodgy' but he reports it is pretty much healed. Markedly inflexible hamstrings which he himself names as his injury risk — 'That's where the injury is going to come from probably if I don't get more flexible.' Self-speculates about ADHD ('maybe I have ADHD. I don't know'), undiagnosed. No conditions, medications or clinician involvement disclosed — the rep never asked.

signals: Lost ground over a long sedentary stretch and is mid-recovery — 'I used to be a lot heavier than I am. I've lost a pretty significant amount of fat'
Explicit regret about what the lost years cost him — 'I was too fat to do like that... I lost some time because of that and some cool stuff'
Wants a former capability back — high-school football was 'probably when I was in the best shape of my life. I would say I was built for some endurance then. I'd like to get some of that back'

Alternative read is the_preserver: 61 years old, high nominal income, framing everything around function at 70 ('I don't want to be the 70 year old who watches TV'). Rejected because he is actively trying to gain 30 lb of fat loss and endurance rather than hold a line, and because he is not medically managed.
Not the_optimizer despite the income and low price resistance — at 260 lb he is not starting from already-fit

goals.text: Lose about 30 more pounds of fat on top of what he has already lost
Build endurance, which he says has never been his strength — 'I've always been built for maximum force over short periods'
Improve flexibility, especially hamstrings, to avoid the injury he thinks is coming
Be functionally capable into old age — 'I see old people who can't move, and I don't want to be one of them'
Hike the Appalachian Trail and long distances with a pack, with his wife, in his late 60s or at 70
Reach a state where he can say yes to any physical opportunity without wondering if he is able — 'I want to be able to say, look, that looks awesome over there. Let's go do that thing'
Learn kettlebell training properly rather than self-educating — 'I'm an infant when it comes to training with kettlebells'
Look better — 'plus I want to look better just like everybody'
Build a durable morning training habit rather than a short-term push

pains.text: Procrastination and no external accountability — 'I need somebody to hold me accountable, because that's my main moral weakness'
Splits attention across too many interests and finishes none — 'I tend to focus on a million things and then I don't follow through with a lot of them'
Talks himself out of training after long office days — 'it's easy to talk yourself out of working out when you get home because I'm tired'
Cannot string together six weeks of morning workouts to build the habit
Knowledge ceiling — has a fully equipped home gym he cannot fully use: 'I just don't have the knowledge, necessarily, to utilize it'
Hamstring inflexibility he expects will cause an injury
Acute time pressure from age — 'at some point you realize that you have more years behind you than you do in front of you and you can't waste any more time'
Has missed shared experiences with his wife because he was not fit enough — 'my wife likes to hike. We don't do it as much'
Fear of a joint injury ending progress — 'I know one bad lift could really mess up one joint, and that would set me back'
Ongoing basement flood remediation at home described as 'an ongoing nightmare' and 'a donkey ride through hell'

objections.raw_quote: Okay. All right. Well, I'll talk it over with the wife, see what she says. You know, I can't just spend that kind of money without talking to her. But I mean, that's around what I expected it to be. So it's not earth shattering.
objections.rep_response: Did not address it at the time — kept presenting the programme for another ten minutes. When it returned, the rep ran the first OB move ('do you feel it would work for you?'), asked how he planned to explain it to her, then coached him on how to pitch it to his wife using a value seesaw. Never asked whether she would object to him being stronger, never separated needing her input from asking permission, and never offered the scripted deposit-with-refund.

objections.raw_quote: Just don't make any decisions right away. I got to think things. But I like the presentation and I'm intrigued.
objections.rep_response: Ran the opening isolation question — 'as far as working with Trevor and the program, what you know about it now, do you feel it would work for you?' — got a strong yes, and then let the stall stand rather than driving to a decision.

objections.raw_quote: Oh yeah, I have no doubts on that score. It's just 9,000 bucks. I got to make sure it's in the budget, that's all.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it once at the end — 'Is there anything else that's coming up for you, maybe around the price or like anything else as far as like any possible hesitations?' — and accepted 'no' at face value. No financial-picture questions and no payment plan structured live despite having already told him plans exist.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Stated verbally, never structured: interest is added on 12-month splits ('for the 12 months, we do add like a little bit of interest to it if people split it up'), internal splits run to a maximum of six months ('you could split it up up to six months. It's usually the longest that we split up internally'), plus third-party financing month to month. Interest rate, instalment amount and total were never quoted.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: No formal guarantee. The rep instead made an unconditional outcome claim: 'our whole goal is that you've dropped at least 10% body fat' and 'So that's the big thing. It's dropping the body fat. It's 100% going to happen.'

evidence: No verbal agreement and no payment link: 'I'll talk it over with the wife, see what she says.'
Deferred deliberately: 'I'm not going to need knee jerk reaction on that, but I'm definitely intrigued and highly interested.'
Only next step agreed was an email from the rep: 'do me a favor and shoot me an email. So I have your contact info and I'll get back to you soon.'

Strong positive signals — full belief in the programme ('Oh yeah, I have no doubts on that score'), price met expectations ('that's around what I expected it to be. So it's not earth shattering'), and the spouse already follows Trevor.

Counter-evidence against optimism: no follow-up call was booked and the prospect controls the next contact entirely; the rep did not close the loop with a scheduled time despite the prospect saying he would speak to his wife within one to two hours.
outcome.next_step: Rep to email contact details; prospect to speak to his wife the same day ('within the next hour or two') and get back to the rep. No follow-up call scheduled.

notable.note: The strongest-intent prospect in this batch and it was left on an email. He believed in the programme outright, found the $9,000 within expectation, had a spouse who already follows Trevor, and said he would talk to her within two hours — and the rep booked nothing, took no deposit and offered no payment link. Separately the rep told a 61-year-old, 260 lb man that dropping the body fat is '100% going to happen' and never asked a single health-conditions question in 48 minutes. The rep also introduced himself as 'one of Boris, freaking Trevor's head coaches', a slip suggesting he is closing for more than one coaching brand.

quality.notes: Regular short-turn swaps; several rep lines are attributed to the prospect and vice versa. Clear examples: 'Well, I got some notes about you' at 00:01:26 is labelled Dan Sigman but is plainly the rep; the summary block at 00:10:37 ('So when you said your goal was to hike, for example, the Appalachian Trail') runs across both labels mid-thought; and 'Make sense so far?' at 00:36:30 is labelled to the prospect but is the rep's check. Roles resolved from content. Height was never captured. The prospect's weight is self-estimated and stale ('I haven't weighed myself in a while. I think I'm around 260').
